clauses.why: Only arises from the spec's multiple-conversation model; the request asks for a bot, not managed separate conversations.
Persisting conversation history across sessions is not called for; an ephemeral chat bot fully delivers what was asked.
An initial screen with an input and no error is true of any chat product; it settles nothing a builder must act on.
A browsable, reopenable conversation history list is a capability beyond a Grok bot.
Multiple stored conversations with a new-conversation action go beyond the request; a single chat suffices.
Since Winter '20, callout time is excluded from the concurrent long-running Apex limit, so bot callouts are not long-running requests by virtue of waiting.
A per-conversation message cap only matters because the spec introduced persisted conversations; context is already bounded by C-4.
Per-user privacy of stored conversations arises only from the spec's added persistence of history.
A third-party processing disclosure is a duty the request does not call for in a development org bot.
Making the model admin-configurable is added work; a builder can simply pick one model and deliver a working bot.
Diagnosing an invalid model setting only arises from the extra configurable-model capability.
Idempotent redeployment preserving data and settings is an operational duty beyond creating the bot.
Cross-version data compatibility assumes versioned releases and persisted history, neither of which the request calls for.
Rollback with data preservation is an operational capability beyond the request; ordinary deploys don't delete fields anyway.
75% coverage is a production deployment rule; deploying to a development org does not require it.
